title: A Pretty Sacrifice
summary: Bring the king closer, then sacrifice the rook to make the opposing queen run out of useful checks.

nodes.question: How can White coordinate pieces that are far apart?
nodes.explanation: White has Ke1, Qa2 and Rb1 against Kh1, Qa8 and Rg8. Moving the king uncovers a first-rank rook check.

branches.title: The queen accepts the rook
commentary: Begin at the complete six-piece source root. The two captures of the checking rook lead to different mating nets.
Kf2+ uncovers Rb1’s first-rank check while bringing the king toward the enemy king.
Kh2 is the only legal king escape from that discovered check.
Rh1+ offers the rook to either the king or queen. Both captures change the geometry.
Qxh1 removes the rook but draws the black queen to h1.
Qxg8 removes Black’s rook. The queen on h1 has no safe checking move against Kf2.
Qb1 is the source’s illustrated waiting move. This is one selected defense, not a claim that the queen has only one legal move.
Qg2# mates: Kf2 protects the queen and closes g1/g3 while the queen covers the remaining flights.
branches.explanation: Qg2# mates: Kf2 protects the queen and closes g1/g3 while the queen covers the remaining flights.

branches.title: The king accepts the rook
commentary: Compare the other capture of the offered rook in the saved source variation.
Kf2+ discovers the rook check and improves the king.
Kh2 steps off the first rank.
Rh1+ brings the rook next to the king with check.
Kxh1 accepts the rook and returns the king to the corner.
Qb1+ checks along the first rank and prepares the h-file finish.
Kh2 is the illustrated king escape. Other legal resources are outside this selected branch.
Qh7# mates down the h-file. Kf2 covers g1, g2 and g3, denying the black king an exit.
branches.explanation: Qh7# mates down the h-file. Kf2 covers g1, g2 and g3, denying the black king an exit.

branches.title: Exchange queens immediately
commentary: Compare the tempting direct queen capture before improving the king.
Qxa8+ trades away the queen with check and gives up the win.
Rxa8 recaptures. The remaining rook-versus-rook ending is exactly drawn with best play.
branches.explanation: Rxa8 recaptures. The remaining rook-versus-rook ending is exactly drawn with best play.

branches.title: Advance the king again
commentary: Compare another discovered check instead of the rook sacrifice.
Kf2+ starts the winning plan.
Kh2 reaches the critical choice.
Ke3+ gives away the win: it uncovers Qa2’s second-rank check while leaving Qa2 exposed to Black’s queen on a8.
Qxa2 answers the rook check by blocking the second rank and captures White’s queen. The exact remaining position is a Black win.
branches.explanation: Qxa2 answers the rook check by blocking the second rank and captures White’s queen. The exact remaining position is a Black win.

exercises.prompt: Why does bringing the king to f2 matter?
exercises.answer: It uncovers a rook check and covers g1, g2 and g3. Those controlled squares later make the queen mates work.

startContext: Begin from the complete six-piece board at zero seconds. The rook sacrifice, both captures and two errors are checked. Only selected source variations are encoded.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
